entries.title: Teldrassil
body: A World Tree grown in the Veiled Sea off Kalimdor's north-western coast, so vast that its crown holds a whole land of twilit forests, streams, lakes and hills, with Darnassus, the capital of the night elves, in its western boughs. Its waterways are fed by the dew the great tree gathers. Its name means "Crown of the Earth".

Teldrassil is young, grown only after the Third War, and it is not well. A sinister presence has crept into it. Furbolgs and grell have gone mad, satyrs have appeared in its glades, and the timberlings that tend its forests have turned savage. Even the turtles and threshers of the surrounding sea have begun fleeing the tree to beach themselves and die on the shores of Darkshore.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg: Teldrassil (introduction, Birth, World of Warcraft, Geography)

entries.title: Shadowglen
body: A small twilit glade in the north-east of the tree, bathed in quiet dusk and ringed by mountains, with only a narrow gap to the south. It is where young night elves begin their training, sheltered from the world.
At its heart rises Aldrassil, a great tree within the great tree.

entries.title: Aldrassil
body: The great tree at the centre of Shadowglen, hollowed and built into a home and training hall. From its top, Tenaron Stormgrip sends the most promising young night elves out into the wider world.

entries.title: Shadowthread Cave
body: A cave in the north-western corner of Shadowglen that has always been home to Teldrassil's great spiders. Lately they have grown increasingly hostile, and the largest of them, Githyiss the Vile, has been the bane of more than one young kaldorei.

entries.title: Dolanaar
body: A night elven village in central-eastern Teldrassil, just south-west of Shadowglen. Its central position puts it at the heart of the tree's affairs, and it is the first real town most young night elves reach after leaving Shadowglen.
The druid Tallonkai Swiftroot leads the fight here against the corrupted furbolgs and satyrs of the tree.

entries.title: Fel Rock
body: Once a beautiful cave just north of Dolanaar, now corrupted and infested with grell. It is the lair of the satyr Lord Melenas, whose kind are night elves twisted long ago by the demons they served.

entries.title: Starbreeze Village
body: A small night elven village south-east of Shadowglen, now overrun by corrupted furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe, an open sign of the demonic infection bleeding into Teldrassil.
A creature called Ferocitas the Dream Eater haunts its outskirts.

entries.title: Ban'ethil Barrow Den
body: One of the sacred barrow dens the night elves built to hold the sleeping Druids of the Talon while their spirits wander the Emerald Dream. It lies at the back of Ban'ethil Hollow, a ravine south of the road from Dolanaar to Darnassus.
The corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs have taken it over, and ambush travellers on the road above.

entries.title: Lake Al'Ameth
body: One of the largest lakes in Teldrassil, just south of Dolanaar, with little more than a small jetty on its shores. Enraged timberlings have been seen along its banks, and it is no longer safe.
Denalan keeps a small camp beside it, studying the strange affliction seeping into the tree.

entries.title: Gnarlpine Hold and the Cleft
body: Gnarlpine Hold, in the far south-west of Teldrassil, was the home of the Gnarlpine furbolgs. Corruption has taken it, and demons now gather there.
The Cleft, north-west of Dolanaar, is another of their dens. Under Ursal the Mauler, its furbolgs ambush travellers on the road to Darnassus and have taken slumbering druids captive.

entries.title: Pools of Arlithrien
body: A cluster of small pools in western Teldrassil, south of the entrance to Darnassus. Once peaceful, they are now prowled by hostile beasts. The night elves abandoned the moonwell here for fear of the Gnarlpine furbolgs.

entries.title: The Oracle Glade
body: A shrine in north-western Teldrassil around the Oracle Tree and the first and most powerful of Teldrassil's moonwells. The Oracle Tree's boughs are shaped like a great eagle perched on a mighty bear; many whisper it was grown by nature magic.

The Oracle Tree has watched Teldrassil's growth alongside the druids, and reports to Archdruid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus by shedding pieces of inscribed bark. Bloodfeather harpies have nested nearby and threaten it.

entries.title: Wellspring Lake
body: A small lake north-east of Darnassus, fed by a spring deep within the World Tree. The Wellspring River drains it north and cascades over the edge of Teldrassil to the sea far below.
It was a favourite spot for night elven fishermen. Now corrupted timberlings walk its banks, and nightsabers and spiders infest the land around it.

entries.title: Rut'theran Village
body: The port of Darnassus, at the very foot of the World Tree, between its roots. A glowing portal carries travellers up into the city, ships sail to the mainland and to the draenei's isles, and hippogryphs fly from its roost to Darkshore.
Since the island is far from the rest of the world, nearly everyone who comes to Darnassus comes through Rut'theran first.

entries.title: Fandral Staghelm
body: The Archdruid of Darnassus, who leads the Cenarion Circle while Malfurion Stormrage lies lost in the Emerald Dream. In the War of the Shifting Sands, a thousand years ago, he lost his only son, Valstann, to the qiraji general Rajaxx.

Fandral was one of the architects of Teldrassil, and believes the night elves' future demands expansion and military strength. His radical views and aggressive manner often bring him into open quarrel with the High Priestess, Tyrande Whisperwind.

entries.title: Tallonkai Swiftroot
body: The druid of Dolanaar who leads the effort to fight back the corrupted furbolgs and satyrs of the Great Tree.

entries.title: Denalan
body: A druid who keeps a small camp beside Lake Al'Ameth, trying to understand the nature of the strange affliction seeping into Teldrassil. The timberlings he studies were meant to tend the forest; now they attack anyone who comes near.

entries.title: Ursal the Mauler
body: The leader of the Gnarlpine furbolgs of the Cleft. Under him the corrupted tribe ambushes travellers on the road to Darnassus and holds slumbering druids captive.

entries.title: After Hyjal
body: At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, at the end of the Third War, the night elves gave up the first World Tree's gift, Nordrassil's power, to destroy Archimonde, and with it their immortality. Soon after, Malfurion Stormrage was trapped in the Emerald Dream, and Fandral Staghelm took leadership of the Cenarion Circle.

Fandral convinced the Circle of Ancients that the time had come to grow a new World Tree and win back what they had lost. Together the ancients and the druids grew Teldrassil in the Veiled Sea, and the night elves made their new home in its boughs.

entries.title: A Tree Without Blessing
body: Nordrassil was blessed by the Dragon Aspects at its planting, and Nozdormu's blessing was the source of the night elves' immortality. Teldrassil received no such blessing. Nozdormu saw the elves' wish to regain their immortality as arrogance, and refused.

A World Tree is bound to the health of the world around it. One that is not well cannot keep the balance between nature and decay, and without the Aspects' protection, Teldrassil is vulnerable to whatever darkness reaches it. The druids watch the tree's growth closely, and many fear what they are seeing.

entries.title: The Fel Moss
body: The corruption spreading through Teldrassil shows itself in many ways: furbolgs gone mad, grell crawling out of the caves, satyrs reappearing in the glades, and a fel moss that grows on the timberlings and turns them savage.
Its source remains a mystery. The druids are studying the affliction from their camps across the tree, but so far no one can say where it comes from.
